summary: Ubuntu LTS provisioning stalls: systemd-resolved split-horizon DNS prevents hybrid AAD device registration
description: Summary: Dev workstation provisioning using the corporate Ubuntu LTS image stalls during the hybrid Azure AD device registration step. The process times out waiting for device enrollment and SSO token exchange. We have consistently reproduced this on hardware that receives split-horizon DNS via systemd-resolved (local stub resolver) and a corporate DNS policy that returns internal IPs for AAD/IdP endpoints.
impact: New hire and swap laptops in staging cannot complete provisioning; image hangs ~10-12 minutes, blocking fleet onboarding. Affects staging autopilot-like fleet rollouts for Linux dev workstations only. No P0 customer impact but impacts onboarding SLAs for a few teams.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Boot machine from corporate USB auto-imaging stick with Ubuntu 22.04 LTS golden image

2) Image runs provisioning script to configure network (DHCP + corporate static DNS via DHCP option 6), installs cloud-auth packages and starts hybrid AAD registration (waagent/adcli/sssd + intune device enrolment hook),
3) systemd-resolved is enabled by default and answers DNS queries on 127.0.0.53; corporate DNS zone returns internal IP for login.company.internal which is used by our IdP discovery endpoint

4) Provisioning script attempts device registration (device-join -> token negotiation -> certificate enrollment). The HTTPS calls to the IdP resolve to internal-only IPs via split-horizon and fail to connect to the IdP from the provisioning container, causing timeouts and the script to retry until overall provisioning process stalls.
observed_logs: Mar 10 09:12:41 provisioning-script[2153]: Starting hybrid AAD device registration
Mar 10 09:12:43 systemd-resolved[412]: Using stub resolver on 127.0.0.53 for interface eth0
Mar 10 09:12:44 curl[2234]: (7) Failed to connect to 10.10.10.24:443; Connection timed out

Mar 10 09:14:01 adcli: ERROR: unable to reach IDP endpoint https://login.company.internal/. Discovery returned private IP 10.10.10.24 which is unreachable from provisioning container network namespace
Mar 10 09:20:00 provisioning-script[2153]: Device registration attempt 6 failed; aborting and leaving machine in REQUIRES_MANUAL_ACTION state
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: systemd-resolved stub resolver is returning split-horizon answers destined for internal networks that are not reachable from the provisioning container, causing registration to fail. When queries bypass stub resolver and use upstream 8.8.8.8 the IdP resolves to a public IP and registration succeeds.
Reproduced in lab: toggling /etc/systemd/resolved.conf DNSStubListener=no allows provisioning to resolve IdP to public IP and completes registration within 45s.

Tested workaround: modified netplan config to set nameservers: [8.8.8.8] in provisioning environment — registration succeeded. However this is not acceptable long-term because it bypasses corporate split-horizon needed for other services.

Checked related packages: sssd/adcli/azure-identity hooks are up-to-date in golden image (adcli 0.8.0, sssd 2.9). No TLS cert issues observed. Container network namespace used by provisioning script does not have route to 10.10.10.0/24 internal net, so internal IP responses are unreachable.

Reviewed current netplan/NetworkManager config in golden image: systemd-resolved enabled by default with DNSStubListener=udp and DNS via DHCP retained. Provisioning container uses host resolver by default which returns split-horizon answers.
attempted_actions: 1) Re-ran provisioning with systemd-resolved disabled -> success (manual workaround for affected machines).

2) Opened internal ticket with Network team to confirm whether provisioning VLAN should receive internal-only DNS responses. Network confirmed DHCP option 6 is intentionally returning split-horizon entries for management VLANs.
3) Created local hosts override during provisioning to point login.company.internal -> public IP (temporary), registration succeeded.
4) Eng Spike: evaluated adding logic to provisioning script to detect unreachable internal IPs and fall back to external discovery endpoints if necessary.
root_cause: Provisioning environment resolves IdP discovery DNS to internal-only IPs via systemd-resolved stub resolver, but the provisioning container/network namespace lacks routes to the internal network, making those IPs unreachable and causing hybrid AAD registration timeouts.
recommended_long_term_fix: Option A: Update golden image provisioning scripts to perform reachability check after DNS resolution. If IP is unreachable, attempt discovery against public endpoint (fallback behavior) for the duration of provisioning.

Option B: Adjust network/DHCP for provisioning VLAN to provide management DNS that resolves IdP to the public address during imaging windows. Requires coordination with Network team and change window.

Option C: Provide a provisioning-specific systemd-resolved drop-in that forwards certain domains (login.company.internal, idp.company.internal) to predefined upstream resolvers or disables stub listener only inside the provisioning runtime.
Proposed priority: implement Option A in provisioning script as a low-risk rollout, followed by Option C in next golden image build for consistent behavior.
resolution: Workaround applied: Updated provisioning script to perform DNS reachability checks and fall back to public discovery endpoints when internal IPs are not reachable. New script uploaded to staging provisioning image. Network team will schedule DHCP scoping discussion to evaluate Option B.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Patch pushed to staging provisioning server: provisioner now runs `ip route get <ip>` and falls back to public discovery when internal IP is not reachable.
2026-03-13: Verified with 12 test devices in eu-west staging; all completed provisioning end-to-end within expected time (median 2m30s).
Follow-up: Add unit test to provisioning harness that simulates split-horizon responses and validates fallback behavior before each golden image release. Assigned to engineering image team.
